title: Orthogonal Quantum Krylov Diagonalisation
authors: Hadi Rammal, Alexandre Perrin, Oumaya Ladhari, Clément Dutreix, Jérémie Messud, Matthieu Saubanere
abstract: Quantum subspace-diagonalization methods, particularly Quantum Krylov Diagonalization (QKD), provide a promising route for computing low-energy spectra of quantum many-body Hamiltonians. However, existing quantum Krylov approaches rely on non-orthogonal Krylov bases, requiring overlap-matrix regularization that limits numerical stability and accuracy. In this work, we introduce an Orthogonal Quantum Krylov Diagonalization (OQKD) framework that reformulates the classical Lanczos recursion at the operator level, enabling an orthogonal quantum implementation of Krylov-subspace diagonalization. By expressing Lanczos vectors as polynomial transformations of the Hamiltonian, OQKD reproduces the orthogonality, tridiagonal structure, and convergence behavior of the classical Lanczos algorithm thus eliminating the need for overlap-matrix regularization. We further show that the required Lanczos polynomials can be implemented using block encoding and Generalized Quantum Signal Processing with the same asymptotic query complexity as Chebyshev-based QKD methods. Numerical simulations of the $J_1$--$J_2$ Heisenberg model confirm the classical Lanczos convergence and numerical stability of the proposed method, while the measurement-complexity scaling is established analytically. Building upon the OQKD framework, we then introduce a restarted state-preparation protocol that replaces a single high-degree polynomial transformation with a sequence of fixed low-degree transformations, maintaining an affordable block encoding success probability while retaining comparable convergence. These results establish OQKD as an orthogonal quantum analog of the classical Lanczos algorithm and identify the restarted protocol as a promising state-preparation strategy for Quantum Phase Estimation.
summary: The paper introduces Orthogonal Quantum Krylov Diagonalization (OQKD), an algorithm designed to compute low-energy spectra of quantum systems by mimicking the stable Lanczos procedure. OQKD achieves this orthogonality directly on the quantum computer, bypassing the need for numerically unstable overlap matrix calculations inherent in prior methods. This establishes a robust and scalable framework for both eigensolving and state preparation protocols like Quantum Phase Estimation.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a quantum algorithm for finding low-energy spectra of many-body Hamiltonians that maintains the numerical stability and orthogonality properties of classical Lanczos methods without requiring overlap-matrix regularization.
main_result: The Orthogonal Quantum Krylov Diagonalization (OQKD) framework successfully implements an orthogonal analog of the Lanczos algorithm, eliminating the need for overlap matrix inversion. Furthermore, a restarted protocol is proposed that maintains convergence while keeping state preparation probabilities affordable.
method: The authors reformulate the classical Lanczos recursion at the operator level, utilizing Generalized Quantum Signal Processing (GQSP) and block encoding to generate an orthonormal Krylov basis directly on the quantum computer.
model_or_system: The method is tested using numerical simulations of the J1–J2 Heisenberg model. The core mathematical structure involves projecting the Hamiltonian onto a reduced subspace spanned by the Krylov basis vectors.
key_observables: Overlap matrix condition number ($\kappa(S)$), energy error convergence, and state preparation fidelity/success probability.
important_parameters: Subspace dimension ($D$), Lanczos coefficients ($\alpha_k,  eta_k$), and the degree of polynomial transformation required for state preparation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing recurrence relations for Lanczos coefficients and utilizing the GQSP framework to implement high-degree polynomial transformations efficiently.
figures_summary: Figures compare QKD/CQKD (showing ill-conditioned overlap matrices) against OQKD, demonstrating that OQKD maintains orthogonality. Other figures show OQKD reproducing classical convergence and illustrating the performance of the restarted state-preparation protocol.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of standard quantum Krylov methods due to non-orthogonality. It then introduces OQKD by reformulating the Lanczos recursion at the operator level, detailing its implementation via GQSP. Finally, it presents a restarted state-preparation protocol and validates the entire framework using numerical simulations on the J1–J2 model.
why_interesting: This work provides a significant algorithmic improvement for quantum eigensolvers by directly addressing the fundamental stability bottleneck (overlap matrix regularization) that plagues current quantum subspace methods, making it highly relevant for simulating complex Hamiltonians in AMO physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic comparison between conventional QKD/CQKD and the proposed OQKD approach. In QKD/CQKD, the NT × NT Hamiltonian is projected onto a Krylov subspace of dimension D spanned by generally nonorthogonal vectors, which are additionally unnormalized in block-encoding-based implementations. Consequently, a generalized eigenvalue problem involving an ill-conditioned overlap matrix must be solved. In contrast, OQKD projects the Hamiltonian onto an orthonormal Krylov basis, elimi- nating overlap-matrix regularization and improving numer- ical stability.

FIG. 2. Results for the J1-J2 spin model (J1 = 1, J2 = 0.5) with an initial mean-field approximated ground state, com- paring QKD, CQKD, and OQKD. The arrows indicate the first subspace dimension at which the thresholded and un- thresholded calculations begin to differ. (a) Condition num- ber of the overlap matrix S as a function of Krylov-subspace dimension. QKD becomes increasingly ill-conditioned with increasing subspace dimension, while CQKD partially mit- igates this effect through the Chebyshev thresholding tech- nique.
